# The question

## What the client asked

The PI, an anesthesiologist, and their fellow ran a randomized trial of a
licorice gargle against a sugar-water gargle, given shortly before
induction of anesthesia in thoracic surgery with a double-lumen tube. At
the intake meeting (`notes/2026-10-16-intake-meeting.md`) the PI asked:

> "did it reduce sore throat afterwards?"

and also:

> "does it last past the recovery room?"

The intake notes record that they care a lot about the second question and
expect reviewers to ask it. The results are intended for a manuscript.

## How we restated it

- **Primary question.** In adults having thoracic surgery with a
  double-lumen tube, does a licorice gargle five minutes before induction,
  compared with a sugar-water gargle, lower the odds of any sore throat at
  rest thirty minutes after arrival in the recovery room (PACU)? "Any"
  means a score above zero on the zero-to-ten sore-throat-at-rest scale
  (`pacu30min_throatPain`). The PI confirmed this as the primary outcome
  (D-001).
- **Secondary question: does it last?** The population-averaged odds ratio
  for any sore throat at rest at each later assessment: ninety minutes
  after PACU arrival (`pacu90min_throatPain`), four hours after surgery
  (`postOp4hour_throatPain`) and the first postoperative morning
  (`pod1am_throatPain`). One common odds ratio across all four
  assessments is reported as a summary. These analyses are descriptive;
  there is no formal test of whether the effect changes over time (D-002,
  D-003).
- **Not analysed.** Cough, at extubation and at each assessment. The PI
  said it is not of interest (D-004).

## Open questions

Questions we could not answer from the data alone. Each is resolved here or
logged in the decision record.

- [ ] **Swallowing pain.** Should sore throat on swallowing
  (`pacu30min_swallowPain`, recorded at thirty minutes only)
  be a secondary outcome? To ask the client.
- [ ] **Enrolled versus analysed.** The enrollment count was uncertain at
  intake; the codebook gives one. Check it against the number of patients
  in the delivered file, and ask the client to explain any difference.
- [ ] **Patients without postoperative data.** The client thought a few
  patients might have no postoperative data. Check at data receipt.
- [ ] **Preoperative sore throat in the protocol.** Did the trial protocol
  exclude patients with a sore throat before surgery? This plan keeps them
  (D-005); ask the client.
